doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

chapter: Gary Burton and the move east
title: Why he came east: Gary Burton and advice to find someone to play with
summary: Goodwin was with George Shearing in L.A. when Gary Burton called; he had told Burton's group he loved their music and advises students to do the same.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What was your reason for coming east?
And how does that work? You get a recommendation? Somebody recommends you, you happen to cross paths on Fifth Avenue or how does that thing occur?

I was still living in Los Angeles and it was actually that year that Gary called me to play. I was with George Shearing that year, it was the best paying job in jazz. And you know the guys in the more — let’s say less commercial jazz groups were all envious of me and I knew them all, because I made twice as much money as they did, working with George. But I just — you know we didn’t get to play real hard, I did a lot of brushes which was good for me. I learned to play the brushes very well I think. Over the ‘60s I had not hung out with Gary, Steve Swallow, Larry Coryell, Bob Moses. And I liked their music. It was something different. There was only a few — there were only a few what you would call fusion or jazz-rock groups, but Gary’s wasn’t the only one but it was one of the more successful ones. And you know I always liked going to hear them play whenever I could and I told them, you know if you ever need a drummer, you know try me out. I adore your music and I really love to play with you, which is a process that I recommend to all of my student drummers. Find somebody you like, would want to play with, and let them know. They won’t be upset with you.
Oh that’s a great one. I had a question down the road, advice to students, and you just nailed it. Do you ever tell them be aware of what bass player you’re joining?
